A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work. Their complete text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices are readable and support reliable comparison, including matching material moved or renamed in v2.

before.justification: V1 reports original CIFAR-10 experiments measuring denoiser approximation errors, gradient locality, input-transformation responses, and patch-composite outputs.

after.justification: V2 retains original empirical analyses and adds experiments on FFHQ and AFHQv2, flexible patch denoising, and generated-sample similarity.

M1.justification: V1 averages overlapping square patch posterior means with noise-dependent patch sizes. V2 retains this construction as PSPC-Square and introduces PSPC-Flex, which selects non-square patches from network gradient sensitivity maps using time-dependent thresholds (Section 5). This adds a substantive denoising component.

E1.justification: V1 evaluates CIFAR-10. V2 adds denoising and sampling experiments on 64×64 FFHQ faces and AFHQv2 animal images, substantially expanding domain and resolution coverage. The translated and partially noise-replaced input examples from v1 Figure 3 are removed.

E2.justification: V2 adds U-ViT to the CIFAR-10 architecture comparison in Figure 2. It also evaluates a Gaussian denoiser attributed to Wang and Vastola and Li et al. in Figure 6, introducing an alternative generalization mechanism beyond v1's empirical-denoiser comparison.

E3.justification: The 150-noise-level, 10,000-sample CIFAR-10 architecture analysis is retained. V2 adds 40-step schedules and 2,000 samples per noise level and process for FFHQ/AFHQ. It also introduces SSCD evaluation using 1,000 shared initial latents and deterministic Euler sampling (Appendix C.1), materially expanding the evaluation design.

E4.justification: The gradient-locality and patch-size analyses are retained, while v1's translation and noise-replacement case study is removed. V2 adds comparisons testing flexible patch geometry, gradient-derived mask visualizations, and complete sampling-trajectory analyses examining accumulated errors (Figures 6–8).

E5.justification: V1 Figure 6 displays mean MSE with intervals labelled 50% and 95% confidence intervals. V2's replacement Figure 6 removes these intervals and reports mean curves only; its SSCD comparison also reports point averages. This withdraws uncertainty reporting from the central comparison, although v1 does not explain the interval construction.

E6.justification: V2 adds U-ViT results, PSPC-Flex and Gaussian-denoiser MSE curves across three datasets, and complete sampling results. Figure 9 reports average SSCD similarity to neural-network samples of 0.55 for PSPC-Flex versus 0.34 for both optimal and Gaussian denoisers. These are newly reported comparisons; the eight original appendix denoiser grids are retained.

T1.justification: V2 extends the formal composite from square crops in v1 Equation 6 to arbitrary patch sets in Equation 11 and introduces the gradient-threshold cropping definition in Equation 12. The underlying posterior-mean reasoning remains, without new theorems or proofs.

C1.justification: Both versions propose local denoising as a mechanism for diffusion generalization. V2 expands the central contribution to two PSPC variants, claims better approximation than previously proposed methods, and adds the claim that complete PSPC samples share structural similarities with neural-network samples (Abstract, Introduction, and Conclusions).

C2.justification: V1's explanation that patch errors compound into unrealistic samples is retained and elaborated through v2's trajectory discussion. V2 additionally proposes using patch posterior probabilities for training-image attribution and discusses copyright, licensing, and computational-efficiency implications (Section 8 and Impact Statement). The central mechanism and sampling-quality limitation remain.

D1.justification: V2 newly documents nearest-neighbour patch-mean estimation, gradient-map construction using 1,000 samples, flexible-patch thresholds, FFHQ/AFHQ schedules, U-ViT checkpoint conversion, and SSCD checkpoint and sampling instructions. The original DiT training budget and hyperparameter table are retained.

R1.justification: V2 substantially expands positioning against alternative mechanisms, discussing Gaussian-score explanations and distinguishing PSPC's flexible patches from the concurrent square-patch method of Kamb and Ganguli. It also adds discussion of patch-based diffusion training and data-replication research, beyond v1's narrower related-work coverage.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, background, and method narrative are extensively rewritten. Related Work moves from Section 2 to Section 7, the method is reorganized into local mechanisms and PSPC variants, Results becomes a separate section, and the appendices are reordered and expanded.

P2.justification: V2 adopts a two-column main layout, reorganizes image comparisons, moves the composite diagram from the appendix into the main text, and expands Figure 6 into a multi-dataset display. New mask, trajectory, similarity, and schedule figures are added. The eight existing appendix grids are enlarged to one per page rather than newly introduced.

improvement.justification: V2 substantially strengthens evidence for the mechanistic hypothesis through flexible patches, comparisons with a Gaussian alternative across three datasets, and quantitative validation of complete sampling trajectories and outputs. These address v1's narrow empirical scope and lack of quantitative sample-level validation. Removing confidence intervals and the input-transformation case study weakens parts of the evidence, and poor final sample quality persists, but the added methodological and empirical support provides a substantial net improvement.
